answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. In effect, the network makes cheating the most expensive strategy available, which is the closest thing to a Sybil-resistant design that economics allows. Consider a beacon as the anchor of the cost.
